evidence: Acknowledged gap, narrowed to current-result selection (physical artifact overwrite is not specified). DESIGN-NOTES.md:247-259 permits concurrent requests and newly appended transcript work, requires explicit results with transcript identity, processed-through position and summary path, and expressly leaves concurrent/out-of-order result handling open; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:32-34 repeats that contract. Concrete sequence: request A processes transcript through position 100; after resume request B processes through 150. B completes first, A later. If the unresolved completion rule treats the last arrival as current, the recovery reference regresses to coverage 100 despite completed coverage 150. Nothing specified requires choosing the greatest valid coverage or keeping a later-coverage result current. That breaks the stated purpose of indexed transcript summaries for recovery (DESIGN-NOTES.md:228-241; HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:37,139), while the explicit processed-through field makes the missing ordering rule consequential. This is a design gap before implementation, not evidence of existing data loss.
